title: Proper sections on an arbitrary geometric closed fibre of a strict local base
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $R$ a strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field [def-weil-geometric-point], and $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ a morphism sending the unique point to the closed point. Let $p:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be proper [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $i:Z_0\to Z$ and $p_0:Z_0\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ give a cartesian square with $p,t$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], and let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Then the actual restriction $\Gamma(Z,F)\to\Gamma(Z_0,i^{-1}F)$ defined by the adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-finite-section-pullback] is an isomorphism. The extension to $\Omega$ need not be algebraic.

proof.text: Write the ring map of t as φ:R→Ω. The closed-point hypothesis says the inverse image of the zero prime is the maximal ideal of R, hence φ is local. IsLocalRing.ResidueField.lift factors it through κ=R/m. The spectrum of this equality factors t as Spec Ω→Spec κ→Spec R. The Lean proof uses the prime-comap equality and lift_comp_residue.
Apply the henselian-pair section comparison to the maximal ideal of R. This makes restriction to Zκ invertible.

Apply the separably closed field-extension theorem to the underlying set sheaf on Zκ. The canonical module/set inverse-image comparison is invertible and is the adjoint transpose of the forgotten module unit. The homEquiv unit identity identifies the forgotten module restriction with the set restriction followed by this comparison. Thus it is bijective, and ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective makes the module restriction invertible. Transfer from identity-object sections to the chosen terminal object by naturality and terminalIsoIsTerminal.

Use pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso to identify the twice-base-changed fibre with the fibre of t, and use sq.isoPullback for the prescribed cartesian model. For each composite restriction, globalSectionsUpperStarMap_comp identifies the map followed by the inverse-image composition isomorphism with the two successive restrictions. Cancel that isomorphism to obtain invertibility of the map in the statement.
